title: Danaher and Microsoft partner to make lab instruments agent-connected
summary: Danaher and Microsoft announced a strategic partnership to build smart instruments and an interoperable agentic AI platform open to multi-vendor labs. The first application named is Molecular Devices' MetaXpress Acquire AI Assistant for high-content imaging.

claims.text: Press release dated 20 Nov 2026 on Danaher's investor site
More agent-enabled instruments from Danaher businesses planned for 2027; first commercial applications expected in 2026
Preliminary internal company testing on a Leica microscope workflow: novices with an AI assistant took up to 83% less time and up to 68% fewer steps (unverified)
Follows Danaher's NVIDIA collaboration (14 Oct) and its Abcam autonomous-lab plan (7 Oct)

why_it_matters: A second big-vendor agent layer over instruments; for ADME labs the test is whether it opens to non-Danaher LC-MS and liquid handlers, not just imaging.

title: PyLabRobot week: Mantis chips and arm, STAR traverse guard, CLARIOstar drawer
summary: PyLabRobot merged 23 commits from 16 to 22 Nov, mostly v1 Formulatrix Mantis work (one arm for v3/v4, chips, valve sequences) plus PreciseFlex arm and gripper fixes. New labware includes KingFisher 96 deep-well and MicroAmp Fast plates.

claims.text: Mantis: single arm model for v3 and v4 with zone routes and approach paths (#1631); chips, nozzles and per-slot chip spots (#1670); per-chip valve sequences (#1676); chip pick and place (#1677)
STAR v1: X moves first raise low channels and the 96/384 head to a minimum traverse height (#1659)
CLARIOstar v1: the plate holder now follows the drawer in and out (#1678)
16 of the 23 commits carry a Claude co-author trailer (count from git log)

why_it_matters: Mantis nanolitre dispensing and plate-reader drawer state are common ADME-plate steps; the AI-assisted commit share keeps rising.

title: Explainer: how PyLabRobot stops a STAR crashing tips during sideways moves
summary: Before any X move, the new STAR code reads each channel's lowest Z point, raises any below a traverse height, and lifts the 96/384 head to safe Z. Callers can skip the checks; the iSWAP is not yet covered.

claims.text: move_to_x_position raises 'everything low on the arm first, then the arm'; height defaults to default_minimum_traverse_height, and 0 raises nothing
Raises ValueError if a channel cannot be lifted to the required height
perform_safety_checks=False sends the move without reads or raises; a TODO notes the iSWAP is excluded until its safety design is decided
Change: 177 lines added, 65 removed; tests file +64/-3
The low-channel raise already existed for XY moves; this change applies it to X-only moves and adds the head raise

why_it_matters: When an AI agent writes the protocol, guards like this in the driver, not the script, are what keep a mis-planned move from crashing tips.

title: Preprint: $351 add-on turns a Tecan Freedom EVO into a 96-well peptide synthesiser
summary: ParSynt-P, a PTFE vacuum/gas manifold plus worklist software, runs up to 96 solid-phase peptide syntheses per run on a Freedom EVO. Built to make peptide standards for targeted plasma proteomics.

claims.text: Hardware cost $351; synthesis cost $0.23 per coupling and $1.14 per mg crude product (authors' figures, not peer reviewed)
One residue coupling takes 94 min; software generates robot worklists from a peptide sequence table and switches gas and vacuum
Uniformity tested on three fully loaded plates with a NAT/SIL standard pair

why_it_matters: Shows a general pattern: repurpose an existing liquid handler with cheap hardware. Relevant to LC-MS bioanalysis labs needing many stable-isotope peptide standards.
authors: ParSynt-P authors (names not confirmed; bioRxiv page unreachable)

title: Explainer: Google's VERID lets AI agents run a PyLabRobot workcell via a digital twin
summary: Google Research's VERID, built on PyLabRobot, keeps a live digital twin of a liquid-handling workcell; agents must pass every command block through simulation before the robot runs it. Missed in October; covered here as a learning piece.

claims.text: Blog post 'Grounding AI agents in biological reality' dated 16 Oct 2026 (Rao, Sirkovic, Pawlosky)
Digital twin tracks arm geometry, well volumes, reagent identities and tip inventory; services: introspection, time-compressed simulation, multimodal trace logging, safe execution
Agent improved reconstruction of unknown dye mixtures more than 5x across cycles; twin state let it recover from a plate-reader failure without re-pipetting

A separate aptamer study (arXiv 2610.24806) reports bead-corrected hit rates of 42.1% (alpha-thrombin) and 33.5% (myoglobin) by round 3, with humans running pulldown, PCR and sequencing between rounds

why_it_matters: The clearest public template for AI-run liquid handling: state tracking plus mandatory simulation. Same gate an ADME lab would want before agent-run assays.
authors: Blog: Rao, Sirkovic, Pawlosky; arXiv 2610.32755: Delley et al. (15 authors)
